label: adult-s7
summary: The model predicts the chance of a low income (the lower of the census income classes) as a sigmoid of a sum of separate parts (training AUC 0.9099; the explanation reproduces the network to within 6.1e-16). Most of the ranking comes from a linear score in the inputs (training AUC 0.7093 without it): more capital gains, capital losses, schooling and weekly hours, and being married, each lower the predicted chance. On top of it sit a youth hinge that pushes people up to their mid-thirties towards a low income (open for 17,107 training people) and leaves age almost without effect after that, a second, steeper capital-gains slope that opens for gains of about 4640 US dollars (shut for Portugal-born people at the usual threshold), an occupation and education gate that withholds a push towards a low income from executives or managers, the armed forces, farmers or fishers, doctorate holders and people working without pay, and two-valued offsets for single categories (White, Asian or Pacific Islander, other service, seventh-to-eighth grade, eleventh grade, Hungary). The parts add on the logit, so they do not interact. Some rare categories carry very large fitted shifts because their indicators are z-scored: the 64 Colombia-born training people get a mean push of 10.3 on the logit through the occupation gate.
